subject: Model Validation with my own environmental data

messages.author: 54d4981d6bf68eaf
messages.subject: Model Validation with my own environmental data
parts:
Dear list members,

I have read the vignettes and help files, and I have a question that, although it might be explained somewhere, I have not find an answer.

I have read a paper entitled "The potential for behavioral thermoregulation to buffer "cold-blooded" animals against climate warming" published in PNAS. In that study the authors validate their NicheMapR model by comparing the observed (cooper model) and predicted temperatures. If I understood correctly, the predicted temperatures were calculated by providing environmental data collected by a weather station and several dataloggers placed near the cooper model to NicheMapR. Am I right?

I would like to perform a similar calibration experiment using agar models of an anuran species. How can I use my own environmental data to predict core temperatures in NicheMapR?

Thank you a lot in advance,
Cheers,
~u

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Model Validation with my own environmental data
parts:
Dear Urtzi,

Try going through the Microclimate-IO vignette - that sets up the inputs more directly using monthly data for Madison Wisconsin. You could try making a script based on this vignette, substituting your inputs for each of the 12 days it is set up to simulate. I'm in the process of revising a software note for the microclimate model which will go into this in further detail. Also, in the next version there will be scope to add hourly observed environmental conditions into the model (rather than daily minima and maxima).

Best wishes,
Mike
